claims.nodeLabel: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
claims.sourceText: DIA solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211, released via The Black Vault
claims.text: DIA solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211, posted 18 August 2008 by the Virginia Contracting Activity (ZD50), sought advanced aerospace weapon system studies across eleven technical areas with a stated horizon of 2050, naming Dr. James T. Lacatski as Government Project Leader.
DIA's Virginia Contracting Activity (ZD50) issued solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211 on 18 August 2008 with contracting officer Jennifer Sylvestre and Government Project Leader Dr. James T. Lacatski.

claims.sourceText: DIA solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211, v.3, released via The Black Vault
claims.text: Solicitation number HHM402-08-R-0211, posted 18 August 2008 by DIA Virginia Contracting Activity (ZD50), contracting officer Jennifer Sylvestre, Government Project Leader Dr. James T. Lacatski.
'The objective of this program is to understand the physics and engineering of these applications as they apply to the foreign threat out to the far term, i.e., from now through the year 2050.'
The statement of work specifies eleven technical areas including 'spatial/temporal translation', 'signature reduction', 'human interface' and 'human effects'.

claims.sourceText: DIA solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211, posted 18 Aug 2008, released via The Black Vault
claims.text: Lacatski is identified by name as 'Government Project Leader' on the DIA AAWSAP solicitation, the only unredacted appearance of the PM in the procurement record.

claims.sourceText: AAWSAP solicitation full text (v.3), via The Black Vault
claims.text: DIA solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211 for the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program was issued in August 2008 and the full text is public.
The AAWSAP statement of work, dated 22 August 2008, specifies the required advanced aerospace research areas.

edges.label: Anomalous phenomena inside a defence contract
edges.note: The AAWSAP statement of work and its deliverables are the tier-1 basis for treating this material as a programme domain rather than folklore.

edges.label: redacted the PM's name it had already published
edges.note: Lacatski is named in the public solicitation and redacted under 10 USC 424 in every post-award release — a records posture aimed at breaking the link between office and person.

b.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC

edges.label: requirement written to a capability only BAASS held
edges.note: An eleven-topic statement of work including spatial/temporal translation, human interface and human effects, competed for five weeks, awarded to the one firm with a decade of exactly that field practice.

edges.label: Field physics is the propulsion answer
edges.note: DIRD 15 and DIRD 19 are commissioned studies of metric engineering and antigravity - the exotic-physics domain applied to the flight problem.

b.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)

edges.label: Government Project Leader
edges.note: Named unredacted as Government Project Leader on the public DIA solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211; redacted under 10 USC 424 in every later release.

edges.label: Tasking reveals expectation
edges.note: The AAWSAP statement of work and the thirty-eight DIRDs are the tier-1 evidence that a government agency paid for study of the physics a recovered craft would require.

edges.label: Same investigators, later contract
edges.note: Principal investigators from the SRI-era programmes reappear in the AAWSAP deliverables three decades later, carrying the research framing with them.
